title: UOS application profile
description: How one application is run under UOS: its binary, format, architecture, runtime and the runtime's settings (specification section 7.3). A profile must never hold a secret. The uos-runtime validator additionally rejects any key that looks like the name of a credential and any value that looks like a private key or a URL with a password in it; unknown keys are rejected by this schema in any case.

schema_version.description: The version of this schema. Readers refuse a version they do not know.

app_id.description: A stable identifier in reverse-DNS style, lower case. Profiles drafted from a file without an identifier of its own use the local. namespace.

display_name.description: The name shown to the user.

binary.description: The absolute path of the program, package or application bundle.

format.description: The container format of the binary.

architecture.description: The processor architecture of the application's code. universal is a Mach-O file holding several architectures; any is for scripts, installers and Android packages.

runtime.description: The runtime that hosts the application.

runtime_channel.description: The release channel of the runtime.

runtime_version.description: The runtime version the profile is pinned to.

prefix_id.description: The application's own prefix. Required for wine and proton: each application has an independent prefix (specification section 12.2).

sync_backend.description: The implementation of Windows synchronisation primitives to use.

isolation_profile.description: The name of the isolation profile applied to the application.

known_requirements.description: Things the application is known to need, as short tokens such as win32, dotnet or arm-translation.

fallback.description: What to offer when the runtime cannot run the application. A Windows virtual machine can only be offered for Windows software.

test_status.description: Whether the application has been tested with this profile. Compatibility claims need evidence (specification section 2.3).
